subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-agent or grouped foreground command-lane config surface, and what server-controlled aggregate capacity contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public scheduler and config semantics and must coordinate with adjacent hook, subagent, browser, and channel lane proposals.

options.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
options.body: Add default-preserving foreground lane selection with per-lane concurrency and a trusted aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduler RFC
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers design one coordinated lane/concurrency model for foreground agents, hooks, subagents, browser-heavy work, and channel routing.

options.title: Document Separate Gateways
options.body: Decline core foreground lane config for now and document separate gateway instances as the supported isolation pattern for heavy agents.

recommendation.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
recommendation.body: Add default-preserving foreground lane selection with per-lane concurrency and a trusted aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the current command-lane enum and concurrency resolver boundary.
